issues.issue: The direction that the Trustee comply with Investment Company Act requirements if applicable is in tension with Section 3.3(c), which forbids any action that would result in the Trust becoming subject to registration as an investment company.

"[i]f any Trust Assets are not duly claimed" sets no mechanism or time for claiming, and the sentence permitting the Trustee to take "all steps necessary to terminate the Trust ... without further order" sits against the same section's requirement of Bankruptcy Court extension.

The five-year outside date and capped extensions must be reconciled with Section 3.6, which defers final distributions until "liquidation of all assets", and with Section 9.8's rule that the Plan controls on inconsistency.
Limiting the amendment power to "[a]ny substantive provision" implies a different (unstated) rule for non-substantive provisions, and the line between the two is nowhere drawn.

The requirement of Committee approval for amendments conflicts with Section 9.1, which says the Agreement "may be amended to comply with such federal income tax laws" retroactively without naming any approval requirement.
The amendment sentence is in the passive voice with no actor and no procedure, and permits amendments that "may apply retroactively" without limit as to whose rights they may alter.
The unrestricted tax-driven amendment power conflicts with Section 8.1, which permits amendment only by the Trustee upon approval of the Committee.

The Trustee's power to waive privilege "in his or her sole discretion" sits against Section 3.4's statement that no holder may obtain privileged information and against Section 4.1's fiduciary-only limitation on the Trustee's powers.
California law governs "and federal bankruptcy law to the extent applicable", a phrase that does not say which body of law prevails where both bear on a question.

Exclusive Bankruptcy Court jurisdiction lasts only "[f]or so long as the Chapter 11 Case may be pending", leaving Section 3.3(g)'s Bankruptcy Court dispute mechanism without a forum after the case closes.
Notice is "deemed to have been sufficiently given, for all purposes" only if deposited in the mail, with no provision for any other method and no address given for the Committee or the Debtor.
The mail-only notice rule cannot be squared with Section 3.3(f), which expressly permits notices, meetings and approvals by email, including on 24 hours' notice.

"(or if no proof of claim has filed ...)" is grammatically incomplete, and the provision does not say which address governs if a holder has both filed a change of address with the Court and notified the Trustee.

The statement that the Agreement "incorporates the provisions of the Plan" does not identify which Plan provisions are incorporated, and it operates alongside a separate conflicts rule in the same sentence.

This Plan-controls rule is the clause a court would use to resolve the Agreement's internal mismatches — for instance Section 3.6's Class 1 distributions against the Class 2-only recitals, or Section 4.7(a)'s self-set compensation against Section 3.3(d).
